chunks: As for the prostration of the obligatory (Quran) passages, then one says in it: 'There is no god but Allah, truly, truly. There is no god but Allah, in faith and in affirmation. There is no god but Allah, in servitude and in bondage. I have prostrated to You, O Lord, in worship and in bondage, not in arrogant refusal and not in arrogance. Rather, I am a humble, fearful slave, seeking refuge.' And one says the takbir when one raises one's head.

key_terms.تكبير: Saying 'Allahu Akbar' — performed here to conclude the sajda before rising.
key_terms.رِقًّا: Bondage; literally 'slavery' or 'subjugation', expressing the worshipper's total submission before God.
key_terms.سجدة العزائم: The obligatory prostration; required upon reciting or hearing one of the four Quran verses (32:15, 41:37, 53:62, 96:19) that mandate a sajda.
key_terms.مُسْتَجِير: Seeking refuge; one who appeals for protection, expressing dependence on God.
key_terms.مُسْتَنْكِف: One who refuses out of arrogance or disdain — the hadith emphasizes the prostration is done freely, not from compulsion.

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited during the obligatory prostration (sajdat al-'aza'im) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith prescribes the specific supplication (du'a) to be recited during the obligatory prostration (sajdat al-'aza'im) — that is, the prostration required upon reciting or hearing any of the four Quran verses that mandate a sajda (found in chapters 32, 41, 53, and 96). The prayer contains a threefold declaration of Divine Unity (tahlil), each time paired with a different affirmation of the worshipper's state: truthfulness, faith, and servitude. The supplicant then confesses personal humility and need, explicitly denying arrogance or self-sufficiency. The closing instruction to say the takbir upon raising one's head connects this narration to the broader ritual practice described by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) for this assembly.
